checks.name: Pre-Outage Baseline Audit
checks.target: Database baseline prior to KAFKA fault injection
checks.expected: Non-empty baseline database state captured before outage injection
checks.explanation: Capturing the pre-outage database baseline establishes the authoritative ground truth for entity row counts prior to inducing infrastructure failure on KAFKA. This ensures post-recovery audits can mathematically prove existing records were neither mutated, orphaned, nor lost during the fault window.

checks.name: Continuous Synthetic Load
checks.expected: Active HTTP requests dispatched during test window (total_sent > 0)
checks.actual: 120 total requests dispatched across 3 concurrent threads
checks.explanation: In accordance with S4-LD-T-L-02 ('Dependency outage under load'), continuous authenticated HTTP load must be sustained throughout the KAFKA outage and recovery cycles to validate the platform under active concurrency pressure.

checks.name: Outage Signal Capture
checks.target: Event Hubs Kafka entity status & Outbox decoupling during KAFKA downtime
checks.expected: Event Hubs entity transitions to Disabled; Transactional Outbox buffers writes without dropped requests
checks.actual: Entity outage confirmed at 2026-10-24T09:53:19.938767+00:00 (Outbox buffered: 120 2xx OK, 0 drops)
checks.explanation: Confirms that when KAFKA / Event Hubs was taken offline, the broker entity successfully transitioned to Disabled status. Furthermore, pursuant to the Transactional Outbox pattern, ingress HTTP endpoints seamlessly accepted batch submissions and buffered domain events into MySQL without client-facing HTTP 500s or dropped writes.

checks.name: Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
checks.explanation: Measures the operational duration elapsed from the dispatch of the KAFKA service recovery command until the dependency transitioned back to 'Ready'. For Azure MySQL Flexible Server (B1ms tier), stopping deallocates the underlying VM; restarting requires cloud-plane compute scheduling, disk re-attachment, and InnoDB recovery (physical envelope: 300-600s). For Kafka/Event Hubs, entity state toggling completes within <= 180s. The measured MTTR of 18s satisfies the required SLA target.

checks.name: Post-Recovery App Readiness
checks.expected: Probe returns HTTP 200 OK within 180s post-recovery (service restored)
checks.explanation: Verifies that following KAFKA restoration, application containers automatically re-established healthy connection pools and resumed serving HTTP 200 OK without requiring container redeployments.

checks.name: Zero Duplicate Batches
checks.explanation: Audits primary key integrity and idempotent POST handling. When clients experience connection drops or HTTP 503s during an outage, automatic retry policies replay payloads. Idempotency-Key headers and unique database constraints guarantee zero duplicate batch entities are persisted.

checks.name: Zero Duplicate Claims
checks.explanation: Enforces business domain invariant that an e-waste batch must never be accepted or claimed more than once. Distributed transaction isolation and status locks prevented race conditions even during high failure concurrency.

checks.name: Zero Duplicate Impact Metrics
checks.explanation: Validates that the environmental impact analytics pipeline (CO2 savings, precious metal recovery) processed replayed domain events idempotently without creating redundant calculation rows.

checks.name: Zero Orphaned Claims
checks.explanation: Verifies relational referential integrity. Proves that partial transaction rollbacks during the outage never committed a claim record pointing to a non-existent or uncommitted batch record.

checks.name: Outbox Queue Resumption
checks.expected: Outbox records tracked and processing resumed (PUBLISHED/PENDING present)
checks.explanation: Confirms that the transactional outbox pattern reliably buffered domain events during degradation and resumed relaying events to Event Hubs / Kafka without queue corruption or message loss upon recovery.

checks.name: Audit Artifact Completeness
checks.expected: All core audit evidence files generated and non-empty on disk
checks.actual: All 4 core artifacts verified on disk
checks.explanation: Ensures end-to-end operational traceability and non-repudiation. All execution logs, SQL outputs, and recovery traces for KAFKA are persisted to disk to satisfy Jira EWCSB-250 compliance.
